## Example 1.6 {#gac2-example-1-6 .gac-lesson}

Given that

$$f(x)=2x-\frac{1}{(x-2)^2},$$

evaluate $f'(1)$ and $f''(1)$.

<p class="booklet-cue">Example 1.6 · Booklet p. 10</p>

::: notes
7 minutes. Keep the original question unchanged. Write the reciprocal term as -(x-2)^(-2) to make repeated chain-rule differentiation clear.

f'(x)=2+2(x-2)^(-3).

f''(x)=-6(x-2)^(-4).

f'(1)=2+2(-1)^(-3)=0.

f''(1)=-6(-1)^(-4)=-6.

The function and these derivative functions are defined for x≠2. x=1 is valid. Keep the two derivative functions available before evaluating: f'(1)=0 is one value, not the constant function f'(x)=0. It does not make f''(1) zero. The odd and even powers of -1 provide a useful sign check.

Use the hinge responses to decide how much of the first derivative to model and how much of the second to ask students to attempt. Do not classify the stationary point: that belongs to later lessons.
:::
